name: Street Custom 'Rathole' Portable Cutting Kit
description: A compact toolkit containing a plasma cutting wand, pry bars, lock manipulation tools, and hinge pin extractors — everything needed to gain unauthorized entry through walls, doors, floors, or ceilings. The centerpiece is a miniaturized plasma cutter powered by a belt-mounted battery that can cut through standard construction materials including drywall, wood, light steel, and concrete block. The complete kit fits in a messenger bag and allows a single operator to create a human-sized opening through a standard interior wall in under 3 minutes. The kit has become standard equipment for urban exploration, burglary, and tactical entry operations across the lower tiers.
legality: Legal as tools — illegal as burglary kit depending on context

specifications.info: cuts construction steel up to 5mm; 15 minutes cutting time; 3 sizes

story_hooks: A series of burglaries show identical Rathole entry patterns — the same tool kit, the same cutting technique, and the same operator based on the plasma arc characteristics.
A Rathole kit has been modified with a silent plasma cutter that operates below 30 dB — entry can be made through a wall while people on the other side of the room do not hear it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian messenger bag system dominated by a bulky belt-mounted battery pack connected via reinforced umbilical cable to a handheld plasma cutting wand. The wand resembles a modified industrial torch with an exaggerated nozzle housing and diagnostic LED ring. Accompanying tools nest in custom foam: three graduated titanium pry bars (flat, curved, and angled), a leather pouch of lock-picking implements, and a spring-loaded hinge extractor assembly. Overall aesthetic is brutalist—function-first design with exposed cable routing and modular attachment points.
physical_description.dimensions: Messenger bag form factor approximately 45cm × 35cm × 12cm when packed; plasma wand barrel 28cm length; battery belt unit 60cm circumference × 8cm depth
physical_description.weight_description: 3.2 kg total—handheld for the wand during operation, but the battery pack requires a reinforced hip belt for extended carrying. Single operator can manage, though mounting to tactical harness is common
physical_description.primary_material: Messenger bag: synthetic ballistic weave (black/charcoal); battery pack housing: matte aluminum alloy; plasma wand: tungsten carbide nozzle on steel body; pry bars: aerospace-grade titanium
physical_description.finish: Matte black anodized aluminum with scorched heat-stress discoloration around plasma nozzle from repeated use. Cable insulation shows minor abrasion scuffs. Weathered appearance standard—these tools are field-worn, not display items
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominant matte black with steel gray accents; battery pack features faded warning stripe decals (orange/yellow). Plasma arc ignition point glows cyan-white during operation. LED status indicators: green (charged), yellow (in-use), red (low power)
physical_description.interface_elements: Plasma wand: trigger-grip ignition, rotary nozzle adjustment dial, inline power readout LCD (2-inch monochrome); battery pack: belt-mounted dual indicator lights, quick-disconnect connector (armored jack), pressure relief valve; lock tool pouch: labeled compartments with roll-out canvas organizer
distinctive_features: Reinforced umbilical cable with redundant shielding (visible braided mesh underneath fraying insulation)
Plasma nozzle modified with external cooling fins—residual heat scorch marks visible
Custom foam insert molded to kit contents—shows indentation wear patterns and staining from repeated use
Belt-mounted battery pack has mounted holster attachment point for wand when not in use
Lock-pick organizer labeled with worn street-slang nomenclature instead of technical names
Hinge extractor assembly features spring-loaded pin pusher mechanism with visible rust staining
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Street Custom proprietary logo (stylized wrench-and-lightning symbol) stamped on battery pack and canvas bag flap; faint regulatory compliance stamps (GLMZ 2224 certification); no serial numbers visible—likely removed
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but operationally scarred. Plasma nozzle shows carbon buildup from previous cuts. Cable has minor kinks from field coiling. Tool arrangement in foam shows signs of frequent access (some picks permanently displaced). Battery pack exterior has scratches and dents consistent with belt-mounted transport over rough urban terrain
